Thanks for the time this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned:

Success criteria (as discussed)
- Functional: Redwood must support your main inference path (patient-summary extraction + clinical QA).
- Performance: p95 latency < 250ms for 512-token responses under typical traffic; sustain peak bursts without failures.
- Quality: extraction F1 > 0.88 on provided eval set; no increase in hallucination rate beyond baseline.
- Economics: target per-1M-token cost within your budget envelope (we'll model this once we have expected traffic).

Workload / traffic items we need from Acme (attached intake template):
- Average & peak RPS (by endpoint), typical concurrency and burst windows
- Typical prompt + response token lengths (mean, 95th pctile)
- Session/streaming vs stateless request mix
- Any PII/data residency constraints or redaction requirements

Proposed timeline
1) You complete the attached "Acme_Health_Workload_Profile.xlsx" and return by Tue 6/29.
2) Redwood provisions a sandbox trial environment and preloads model + sample cache by Mon 7/5.
3) Run smoke tests and a 3-week evaluation window starting 7/5-7/26.

Owners
- Redwood: Ben Carter (trial lead), Marissa Cole (workload ingestion & monitoring), Dylan Brooks (infrastructure/load tests).
- Acme: Elena Rossi (product), Aaron White (engineering), procurement@acmehealth.com (procurement/contract).

Next steps
- Elena: confirm the success criteria above + return the workload spreadsheet (attached)
- Ben: will provision sandbox and share endpoints + test accounts once we have the sheet

Attachments: POC_evaluation_template.xlsx, Acme_Health_Workload_Profile.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Thanks Ben — great recap. Confirming details from our side and filling out a few numbers to help you size things: 

Confirmed success criteria — we'll treat latency and extraction F1 as the primary gating metrics. A few specifics:
- Typical traffic: avg 5 RPS across peak hours for the patient-summary endpoint; peak bursts up to ~45-60 RPS for short windows (5-10 minutes) during morning syncs.
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 8-12 requests; during peak spikes can reach ~30 concurrent requests across the cluster.
- Token lengths: average prompt ~60 tokens, expected average response ~250 tokens; 95th pctile response length roughly 600 tokens for long summaries.
- Request mix: ~70% stateless requests, ~30% session-based (KV cache helpful).

Timeline looks good — we can return the completed workload spreadsheet by Tue 6/29. Proposed trial window of 7/5-7/26 works for our engineering team.

I've attached our internal load-test plan (acme_load_test_plan.pdf) and a filled-first-pass of the workload sheet (Acme_Health_Workload_Profile.xlsx). Will confirm procurement details next week (Aaron copied).

On the economics side, please include an estimated cost projection for the trial (1M, 5M, 10M token scenarios) and call out any cost-optimized configs you recommend (quantization, batching, caching).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Product Lead, Clinical AI | Acme Health
